damped.d.b: Constant $b$ in the damping force $F_d = -bv$. $b < b_c$ underdamped, $b = b_c$ critically damped, $b > b_c$ overdamped
damped.d.bDrive: Constant $b$ in the damping force $F_d = -bv$; smaller $b$ gives a taller, narrower resonance peak
damped.d.vectors: Velocity $v$ (orange) and damping force $F_d = -bv$ (pink) of the block
damped.d.ratio: Angular frequency $\omega_d$ of the moving support as a multiple of the natural angular frequency $\omega_0 = \sqrt{k/m}$; applies while running
damped.f.goal.env: The damping force $F_d = -bv$ removes mechanical energy: the amplitude decays exponentially as $x_m e^{-bt/2m}$, and the angular frequency drops slightly to $\omega' = \sqrt{\omega_0^2 - \gamma^2}$ ($\gamma = b/2m$)
damped.f.goal.regimes: Comparing $b$ with $b_c = 2\sqrt{km}$: underdamped ($b < b_c$, decaying oscillation), critically damped ($b = b_c$, fastest return without oscillating), overdamped ($b > b_c$, slower return without oscillating)
damped.f.obs.default: Default $b$ = 1.0 kg/s: the oscillation shrinks along the grey dashed envelope $\pm x_m e^{-bt/2m}$, by $1/e$ every $2m/b$ = 2 s
damped.f.obs.energy: $E$ (black) drops in steps: the damping removes energy at the rate $dE/dt = -bv^2$, so $E$ is flat at the turning points ($v = 0$) and steepest through equilibrium. The grey dashed $\tfrac{1}{2}kx_m^2 e^{-bt/m}$ decays twice as fast as the amplitude
damped.f.obs.crit: $b$ = 8.0 kg/s ($b = b_c$ for the default $k$, $m$): the block returns fastest without passing equilibrium (critically damped)
damped.f.obs.over: $b$ = 20 kg/s: no oscillation, and the return is slower than at $b_c$ (overdamped): the larger damping force holds the block back
damped.f.obs.m: A larger $m$ raises $b_c = 2\sqrt{km}$ and the decay time $2m/b$, so the same $b$ lets the block oscillate longer
damped.f.obs.ref: Grey dotted = no damping ($b = 0$), $x_0\cos\omega_0 t$. With damping the period is slightly longer ($\omega' < \omega_0$), more clearly as $b$ approaches $b_c$
damped.f.assume.start: Released from rest at $x_0$ = 0.20 m, so in $x = x_m e^{-bt/2m}\cos(\omega' t + \phi)$ the amplitude is $x_m = x_0\omega_0/\omega'$ ($x_m \approx x_0$ for light damping). The envelope is shown when underdamped, the approximation $\tfrac{1}{2}kx_m^2 e^{-bt/m}$ only for light damping ($b \le b_c/2$)
damped.f.assume.grav: $x$ is measured from equilibrium (up +); gravity only shifts the equilibrium (free-body diagram: spring force $F_s = mg - kx$, $g = 9.8\ \text{m/s}^2$). Damping force proportional to velocity; massless spring and rod
damped.f.assume.arrows: Arrow lengths are relative ($v$ to $x_0\omega_0$, $F_d$ to $kx_0$). RK4 integration (1 ms step); the envelope and reference curves are exact
damped.d.goal.res: Moving the support at angular frequency $\omega_d$ (driving force $F_m\cos\omega_d t$, $F_m = kd$) makes the block oscillate at $\omega_d$ once the transient has died out. The amplitude $x_m$ is largest near $\omega_d \approx \omega_0$ (resonance)
damped.d.goal.b: Less damping gives a taller, narrower resonance peak, of height $\approx F_m/(b\omega_0)$
damped.d.obs.build: Default ($\omega_d = \omega_0$, $b$ = 1.0 kg/s): the amplitude grows from 0 over a few seconds to the dashed $\pm x_m$ = 0.080 m, 4 times the support amplitude $d$ = 0.020 m
damped.d.obs.sweep: Change $\omega_d/\omega_0$ while running: the ring (current amplitude) moves towards the dot on the curve (steady-state amplitude). At 0.5, $x_m \approx 1.3d$; at 2, $x_m \approx 0.33d$
damped.d.obs.b: Grey curves = $b$ 0.5 (solid), 1 (dashed), 2 kg/s (dotted): each doubling of $b$ roughly halves the peak and widens it
damped.d.obs.phase: $\omega_d \ll \omega_0$: the block moves with the support (grey $y_s$, $\phi \approx 0$). $\omega_d = \omega_0$: a quarter period behind ($\phi = 90^\circ$). $\omega_d \gg \omega_0$: opposite to it ($\phi \approx 180^\circ$)
damped.d.obs.ring: Ring = current amplitude $\sqrt{x^2 + (v/\omega_d)^2}$, equal to the dot ($x_m$) in the steady state; during the transient it swells and fades like beats
damped.d.assume.drive: Support amplitude $d$ = 0.020 m: a pin on a turning disk pushes the slotted support, $y_s = d\cos\omega_d t$ (Scotch yoke). The spring force $k(y_s - x)$ gives the driving force $F_m = kd$. The free-body diagram splits it into $F_s = mg - kx$ and the driving force $F = ky_s$
damped.d.assume.start: The block starts at rest at equilibrium. RK4 integration (1 ms step); the resonance curves and the dashed lines are the exact steady state
